targetText:
Whatever the form of the process of production
in a society, it must be a continuous process, must continue to go periodically
through the same phases. A society can no more cease to produce than it
can cease to consume. When viewed, therefore, as a connected whole, and
as flowing on with incessant renewal, every social process of production
is, at the same time, a process of reproduction.
explanation: Simple reproduction shows that capitalism continuously reproduces its own social conditions: workers leave production empty-handed and must return to sell their labor again.

targetText: under its aspect of a continuous connected process, of a process of reproduction, produces not only commodities, not only surplus-value, but it also produces and reproduces the capitalist relation; on the one side the capitalist, on the other the wage labourer.
summary: Reproduction of the capitalist relation: capitalism continuously reproduces both commodities and the unequal class relationship.
explanation: Capitalist production is not a one-off transaction. As a continuous process of reproduction, it inexorably reproduces the structural class divide: the worker exits the production cycle with nothing but their labour-power to sell again tomorrow, while the capitalist exits with accumulated capital to command labour anew.
